reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the cap is measured by "Fees", which the resolved definitions limit to a one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the quantum falls far below the fallback of 12 months' fees and is effectively illusory (walk-away territory), notwithstanding the otherwise sound mutuality and carve-out architecture.

Redline is directionally correct and minimal: it edits only the cap basis in 21.1, substituting "all amounts paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms" in the preceding twelve months with a USD 1,000,000 floor, while leaving the mutual-cap sentence, Excluded Claims (21.3) and the payment-obligation carve-out untouched. Avoiding amendment of the "Fees" definition is the right choice to prevent collateral effects on payment terms.

Comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice: it identifies the illusory-cap defect, states the playbook position, and confirms that indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement remain outside the cap.

Deterministic checks corroborate the edit (12-month/fixed-floor basis present, no unlimited Customer liability, changed-character ratio 0.325 consistent with a targeted basis replacement rather than a section rewrite). No double-flagging of the same commercial term is apparent.
